title: Per-tenant adaptive sampling + exporter throttling shim for OTLP pipelines
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Background: Our hosted tracing ingress sees large variance in incoming span rates across tenants. Heavy tenants cause downstream exporter queueing and occasional 5xx retries on Tempo/Jaeger backends, increasing observability costs and tail latency. Current global sampling and coarse throttles are blunt instruments and hurt signal for mid-size tenants. Goal: implement a tenant-aware adaptive sampling controller paired with an exporter throttling shim that enforces per-tenant fair-share and preserves high-value traces for SLO-critical tenants.

Proposal summary:
1) Implement a lightweight per-tenant sampler that adjusts sample rate based on recent span rates, error-rate signals, and a tenant priority weight. Sampler runs in the trace-ingest path before batching and exports.
2) Build an exporter wrapper (shim) that applies queued-rate-based backpressure: it can delay, drop low-importance spans, or downgrade export batch sizes when an exporter shows elevated latency or errors. Shim exposes metrics and config per-tenant, and supports dynamic throttle policies from a central controller.
3) Provide a control-loop (sampling-controller) that consumes aggregated metrics (ingest rates, export latencies, SLO violations) and pushes sampling/throttle updates via a simple API to the node-local agent.

Design highlights:
- Sampling decisions are deterministic per-span via a tenant-specific reservoir/hash to avoid correlated holes.
- Priority weight for tenants comes from billing/contract data (via metadata), letting us bias sampling to paid SLAs.
- Exporter shim maintains a soft queue with hysteresis and implements a token-bucket style drain to Tempo/Jaeger; when exporter latency > threshold, the shard can selectively drop spans by low-priority attribute (e.g., health-check, 2xx ops).
- All configuration changes are versioned and auditable; controller provides safety caps to avoid catastrophic global drops.

Why different from previous exporter work: existing tickets focused on multi-backend routing, format translation, and fallback. This ticket concentrates on preserving signal quality by adapting sampling per tenant and protecting downstream exporters via graceful throttling (not just failover).
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant sampling implemented in node-local agent: sample rate adjustable via API and persisted per-agent
Exporter shim drops only classified low-value spans under pressure and emits drop-reason metrics
Sampling-controller can push updates and the agent applies them within 5s under normal load
End-to-end e2e tests demonstrate tail latency reduction to backend during synthetic high-volume tenant test by >= 30%
No regression in existing OTLP compatibility test-suite; all CI checks pass
Documentation: runbook and config guide published in Confluence; SDK/agent config examples added
implementation_steps: Add tenant metadata propagation in ingest pipeline and enrich spans with tenant_id where missing
Prototype deterministic per-tenant sampler in agent (C++/Rust shim depending on binary) and expose API endpoint for updates
Implement exporter wrapper with queue + token-bucket drain logic and selective-drop heuristics
Build sampling-controller service (k8s) to aggregate metrics and compute adjustments; expose a push API
Integrate metrics: per-tenant ingest rate, exported batch latency, drop counts, sampled_rate per tenant
Create chaos/e2e test harness to simulate 100x tenant burst and validate behavior
Add dashboards (Grafana) for top-N noisy tenants, drop reasons, and controller decisions
Run canary rollout behind feature flag for 10% of nodes and monitor for 48h before wider rollout
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Deploy agent changes behind feature flag to canary pool (10% infra). Phase 2: Launch sampling-controller in staging, enable for selected low-risk tenants, monitor metrics for 72h. Phase 3: Gradually increase tenant coverage and enable exporter shim thresholds. Phase 4: Default enablement and deprecation of coarse global throttle. Rollback: controller can set sampling to 100% or undo throttles; agents accept immediate policy override.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive sampling may remove signals needed for debugging. Mitigation: Safety floor per-tenant (min_sample_rate) and gradual decay to reductions with audit logs.
Risk: Controller bug may push bad policies. Mitigation: Staged rollout, canary quotas, and an emergency kill-switch that sets sampling to 100%.
Risk: Complexity in tenant metadata mapping for older SDKs. Mitigation: Fallback heuristics and instrumentation work to enrich missing tenant_id in pipeline.
Risk: Exporter shim CPU/memory overhead. Mitigation: Microbenchmarks and limits; shim is designed to be async and bounded.
Risk: Billing/priority weight misuse. Mitigation: Access control on the controller and audit logs for changes.
